review.review: The hero starved to death: decision 4553, accepted log line 12986, advances a wait from 1 HP to 0, and the final public message explicitly confirms starvation. The initiating unresolved work was the strength potion seen behind magical fire at decisions 3990 and 3992 (log lines 11306 and 11312). Recorded routing diagnostics reject access through the fire buffer. At first sighting HP was 66/75, below the unknown-potion test threshold; indigo and amber potions were unidentified. At decision 4438 (lines 12647–12650), the still-uncollected mandatory resource vetoed descent and fallback continued while starving. Source browsing resolves the priority-pickup, puzzle-supply, recovery and descent-veto chain. A snapshot-only probe finds local test banks but does not admit protecting the other carried potions. No patch is proposed: a safe preparation alternative has not been established, and relaxing hazards, guessing potion effects or waiving the mandatory pickup would be unsupported. No post-death identities are treated as earlier knowledge. The unchanged full unittest suite passes 1,546 tests, with four skipped. Offline bookkeeping reconstruction matched recorded actions and reasons through decision 3989, then stopped before selecting 3990 because its scratch state-export step could not serialize immutable configuration. This was not a gameplay crash. The local preparation probe was snapshot-only, not validated recovered runtime memory; no changed-policy continuation was evaluated. No patch or regression is supplied because a safe replacement preserving potion protection and health admission was not established.
review.learnings: Resolve preparation before health and food are exhausted, but require a demonstrated safe test/stash approach or observed non-drinking identification. Keep mandatory strength pickup, actual-effect verification and honest collection evidence. A preparation selection alone would not prove retrieval or survival.
